tasks.title: Provider health contract
tasks.acceptance: A provider with zero observations reports unknown with a null observed success rate and a zero sample count, never a mid-range score and never a pass; any prior used to rank an unobserved provider is labelled as a prior rather than presented as measured availability; degraded-but-usable is a state distinct from up and down; health output is pure over the observations plus an explicit policy version, with no hidden wall-clock decay; and health never affects entitlement, so a provider at perfect health still cannot make an unauthorized candidate eligible

typecheck.evidence: turbo run typecheck --filter @liberty/provider-sdk exit 0 under pinned Node 22 resolved via npx node@22.

unit.evidence: turbo run test --filter @liberty/provider-sdk exit 0 under pinned Node 22: zero observations yielding unknown with a null observed rate and a zero sample count, a prior labelled rather than presented as measurement at the same ranking number as a measured value, the degraded band held distinct from up and down, purity over observations plus an explicit policy version with Date.now replaced by a thrower to prove no wall clock is read, whole-report permutation invariance under generated policies, monotonicity in each count, and a compile-time guard that no health type can carry entitlement.

tasks.title: Media inspection service
tasks.acceptance: Media inspection sits behind its own package boundary rather than inside the provider SDK, because probing is cross-provider I/O plus an external binary with a different security profile; the manifest-parsing path carries no FFmpeg dependency and ships first, reading the declared ladder out of an HLS or DASH manifest without opening a media segment; a fact obtained by probing carries provenance that distinguishes it from a fact merely stated by a provider, and a divergence between the two is preserved rather than collapsed into a fact of unknowable origin; and the service never becomes a general-purpose fetcher, so protocols are allowlisted, egress is confined to an allowlist, hostnames are resolved and private ranges rejected before inspection is invoked, and redirects are revalidated rather than trusted because the first host was allowed

typecheck.evidence: turbo run typecheck --filter @liberty/media-inspection exit 0 under pinned Node 22 resolved via npx node@22.

unit.evidence: turbo run test --filter @liberty/media-inspection exit 0 under pinned Node 22: both manifest formats, whole-ladder extraction, omitted fields becoming null rather than inferred, provenance separating manifest_declared from provider_declared and probe, protocol and egress allowlisting driven by the allowlist constant itself, resolve-and-reject of private ranges before invocation with every resolved address checked, redirect revalidation, bounded bodies and deadlines, a pre-count rendition cap refusing before any ladder is built, and a fast-check property asserting the whole returned object is stable under input permutation.

tasks.title: Auth integration decision
tasks.acceptance: A recorded decision selects the auth approach and states the boundary it implies: a packages/auth seam that the rest of the application depends on instead of the vendor library, database-backed sessions, a deliberately small enabled surface with the advanced plugin stacks left off, and an exact-pinned dependency whose upgrades are treated as security-sensitive work rather than floated on a caret range

tasks.title: Profile model
tasks.acceptance: Profiles are modelled above authentication rather than inside the auth library, with the active profile carried alongside the session rather than inside the identity record; profile scoping is present in the first migration rather than retrofitted, because that is the part that is expensive to reverse; profiles can be created and selected with authorization tests

tasks.title: Progress persistence
tasks.acceptance: Progress rows are scoped to a profile id rather than a user id and keyed by (profileId, contentId) so a repeated write upserts idempotently, with read and write authorized against the active profile; two devices writing the same title are resolved by a server-issued writer epoch rather than by client timestamps or by a monotonically-increasing-position rule, because client clocks are unreliable and a monotonic rule wrongly refuses a legitimate rewind; and writes go directly to PostgreSQL, with no Redis write-behind introduced until a PostgreSQL problem has actually been measured

tasks.title: Watchlist persistence
tasks.acceptance: Typed add, remove, and list APIs with authorization

tasks.title: Playback session API
tasks.acceptance: Server resolves authorized provider candidates and clients cannot submit arbitrary media URLs; the session response is a discriminated union on outcome (granted, denied, unavailable) with reasons present on every branch rather than as an optional field, because a denial with no reason trail violates the reason-trail invariant exactly as much as a grant with none

tasks.title: Player state machine
tasks.acceptance: The machine models the session and candidate lifecycle (resolving, loading a candidate, playing, buffering, seeking, recovering, failing over, ended, fatal) rather than UI state, which the controls layer already owns; the video element and the playback engine stay authoritative and the machine is a validated projection of them, so every engine and media event has an inbound transition even in states where it supposedly cannot occur

tasks.title: Playback telemetry
tasks.acceptance: Startup, rebuffer, quality switch, and failure events are observable with privacy redaction

tasks.title: A/V continuity diagnostics
tasks.acceptance: Browser playback diagnostics detect and report deterministic A/V continuity proxies with their evidence source and reason trail, never label a proxy as measured A/V skew, never expose a millisecond sync-offset claim without an external measurement source, and document the external flash-and-blip procedure for true A/V offset measurement

tasks.title: Recommendation boundary
